title: balsamea habessinica
intro: Balsamea habessinica, commonly known as East African myrrh, is a plant-based resin derived from the Commiphora genus, primarily obtained from Commiphora schimperi. East African myrrh has been used in traditional medicine to treat various health conditions, including wounds, inflammatory diseases, and digestive issues, due to its health benefits of promoting wound healing, reducing inflammation, and exhibiting antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of East African myrrh include its ability to stimulate the immune system, reduce pain and fever, and exhibit antioxidant properties. The bioactive constituents of East African myrrh include terpenoids, such as furanosesquiterpenes, and phenolic compounds, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
